summary: The Bahamas admits citizens of over 100 countries without a visa — normally 90 days, and up to eight months for US citizens — and requires everyone else to obtain a visa from a Bahamian mission before traveling. All arrivals complete an electronic immigration and customs declaration.

fee.notes: Approximate for a single-entry visitor visa; multiple-entry visas cost more. Confirm the current fee with the Bahamian embassy, high commission or consulate handling your application.
Approximate — the Department of Immigration sets extension fees and can grant visitors a total stay of up to eight months; confirm the amount at the office.
Approximate permit fee for a remote worker, plus a smaller application fee; students pay less and accompanying family members are charged separately.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for the whole of your stay. Airlines routinely apply a six-month rule of their own, so travel with at least six months' validity where possible.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required from travelers aged one year and over arriving from — or having recently transited — a country with risk of yellow fever transmission. No vaccination is required if you fly in directly from Europe, North America or the rest of the Caribbean.

travelInsurance.text: Insurance is not an entry condition, but healthcare is private and paid for up front, and serious cases are flown to Florida — cover that includes medical evacuation is strongly advised.

onwardTicket.text: Visitors must hold a return or onward ticket and give the address where they are staying; officers set the length of stay on that basis.

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published. Officers may ask visitors to show they can support themselves, particularly for long stays or when accommodation is not confirmed.

declarations.name: Bahamas electronic immigration and customs declaration (Click2Clear)
declarations.text: Arriving passengers complete an electronic immigration and customs declaration through the Bahamas Customs Click2Clear system — usually a link from your airline or the official government travel page. Fill it in before you fly and save the confirmation; paper cards are still used on some routes.

currencyLimits.text: Cash or negotiable instruments worth USD 10,000 or more (or the equivalent) must be declared to Bahamas Customs on arrival and departure.

notes: Firearms and ammunition are illegal without a Bahamian permit — a single stray round found in luggage or on a yacht leads to arrest and prosecution.
Duty-free allowances are modest (roughly one liter of spirits and 200 cigarettes for visitors aged 18 and over); goods above the allowance are dutiable.
Spear guns, conch and crawfish out of season, and marine products are controlled — check before taking anything home.

payments.text: Cards are accepted almost everywhere in Nassau, Paradise Island and Freeport, and the Bahamian dollar is pegged one-to-one with the US dollar, which is accepted interchangeably. Carry cash for jitneys, straw-market stalls and the Family Islands.

safety.text: Resort areas and the Family Islands are calm, but Nassau and Freeport have significant violent crime concentrated in specific neighbourhoods — avoid the "Over the Hill" area of Nassau, take licensed taxis at night, and treat water-sports operators with care as they are lightly regulated.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Bahamas Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: December to April brings dry, warm days and the calmest seas. Summer is hot and humid, and the hurricane season runs from June to November with a peak from August to October.

idp.text: Bahamas is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

tips.text: Flights to the United States clear US immigration and customs before departure at Nassau and Freeport — you land in the US as a domestic arrival. Allow at least three hours at the airport, and remember that US entry rules (including ESTA) are checked there, not on landing.

June to November is hurricane season, peaking in August and September. Take insurance covering weather disruption and follow official advice — evacuation orders on low-lying islands are issued at short notice.

There is zero tolerance for firearms and ammunition. Travelers, including boaters and cruise passengers, are regularly arrested over a forgotten round in a bag — check every piece of luggage before you fly.
The Bahamas is 700 islands: getting between them means a domestic flight or the mail boat, and schedules are thin. Build a buffer day before an international departure.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for The Bahamas?
faq.answer: Most visitors do not. Citizens of the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, the EU and over a hundred other countries enter without a visa — normally for up to 90 days, and up to eight months for US citizens. If your nationality is not on the exempt list you must obtain a visa from a Bahamian embassy, high commission or consulate before traveling.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a passport for The Bahamas?
faq.answer: Yes for air travel — a valid US passport is required to fly. Closed-loop cruises and some sea arrivals accept a passport card or birth certificate with photo ID, but a passport is the only document that works in every case, including if you have to fly home unexpectedly.

faq.question: Do I have to fill in a form before arriving?
faq.answer: Yes. Arriving passengers complete an electronic immigration and customs declaration through the Bahamas Customs Click2Clear system, usually linked from your airline or the official government travel page. Complete it before you fly and keep the confirmation on your phone.

faq.question: How long can I stay in The Bahamas?
faq.answer: Visa-free visitors are normally stamped in for up to 90 days, and US citizens for up to eight months. The Department of Immigration can extend a visitor's stay to a maximum of eight months in total, for a fee — apply before your current permission expires.

faq.question: Can I work remotely from The Bahamas?
faq.answer: Yes — the Bahamas Extended Access Travel Stay (BEATS) program lets remote workers and students live in the islands for a year, renewable, for a permit fee of roughly USD 1,000. A normal tourist entry does not allow you to work for a Bahamian employer.
